GRMOVER.notes:
Exports rice as a commodity. Key play is that expanding two fold
1. New branded (10x) rice in India. This B2C division is gaining momentum and grew 26% in Dec 2025 quarter
2. They had a tie-up with a large Saudi distributor who will help them distribute their branded rice (10x) in the Kingdom. Recent quarter this seemed to have some traction

Key bet is that it transforms from a commodity exporter to a branded player which will trigger a re-valuation

MAHLOG.notes:
Cannot quite see a massive TAM expansion. Play on company getting better, improving margins. Industry is not showing any great momentum either
Bet on:
1. Auto especially M&M growth
2. Contract logistics and Rivigo Express business picking up

Asset lite logistics player (They hire the truck, warehousing etc but design the E2E logistics solution). Serves 3 key segments
1. Logistics for parent M&M: 50-55% of revenue. Share actually increasing and sensitive to Auto and CV cycle
2. Logistics for other Auto/FMCG/Engg companies. Share 25-30% but slow growing as they exit from thin margin contracts
3. E-Commerce: Share 15%. Flat. Warehousing is growing but last mile delivery business, they are exiting.

Key driver is the Rivigo Express business turnaround. Originally MAHLOG is a contract logistics player (deliver input materials to a particular factory). Rivigo allows it to enter the space of distribution to dealers. The unique part here is that often times a company will not require a full truck for delivery, so Rivigo accumulates the demand in a given hub using it proprietary algorithms. This business profitability is finally turning around and revenue growth is 25%+ (drive by volume growth).

APARINDS.notes:
Bet on revival of the US export growth triggered by FTA and inventory normalization.

Grid modernization play. Manufactures
1. Conductors (50%) including HEC (high efficiency conductors). Largest non-Chinese player in this space
2. Cables (25%)
3. Transformer oil (25%)

Domestic 60-70%. Domestic is growing at 30% driven by India focus on grid up gradation
Exports have been de-growing at 10-15% which is a headwind for the stock. Export business has much higher margin

EBGNG.notes:
Takes old laptops (75%) and desktops. Refurbishes them and sells them. Primarily a B2B play. 
Supply of laptops comes from corporates. It refurbishes and sells them back.

Export oriented (75% of sales). They have refurbishment centers in India, Middle East and US.
Trigger seems to be that with growing AI adoption in enterprises, they are looking to refurbish older laptops and desktops.

PAISALO.notes:
Originates, services and collects the loan in a co-lending framework with PSBs (especially SBI). Focussed on rural areas and Tier 3-5 cities. Customer profile is bottom of the pyramid (small shopkeepers, vegetable vendor, dairy farmer). They keep 20% of the loan on their book and the rest is on the PSB books making it an asset lite model.

Credit growth seems to be slowing for the last few quarters though high at 16%. GNPA is low (0.83%) but stable.

Equitas/Ujjivan maybe a better way to play the "Bharat Lending" story. They have a tailwind for improving GNPA and accelerating credit growth

RAIN.notes:
Produces CPC (Calcined petroleum coke) and CTP (Coal Tar pitch) which are used in the aluminum smelting process and graphite electrodes in steel EAF. Input is GPC (Green petroleum coke) which is a by-product of the refining process. 

Bets are:
1. Aluminium bull market. If smelters in EU and US pick up, RAIN is a massive winner
2. They could expand into EV anode production. 

Risks:
1. High Debt

SEAMECLTD.notes: Diving support vessels for offshore oil fields. 95% of revenue comes from ONGC. Linked to their Capex cycle. Given they are the only Indian operator with these vessels they have right to first refusal in any BID. So they can match the highest bid and win the volume. Global rates for DSV's have risen and that is a tailwind to the stock. Some recent contracts indicate they are evolving from an asset renter to providing EPC services which have higher margin.

IMFA.notes:
Ferro chrome producer. Owns and operates the underlying chromite mine as well. Electricity makes 50% of the cost and they have captive power plants.
Used in manufacturing stainless steel.

South Africa is one of the largest producers of Ferro chrome. Their industry is going through a turblent period due to high energy prices. This is a tailwind for ferro-chrome pricing. They used to make up 30% of the global production which is being cut my more than half. 

Acquiring tata steel plant. This will add 1.5L tonnes to their current 2.8L tonnes. Could generate close to 90cr in PAT quickly. Another Greenfield expansion in same location of 1L tonne.

Domestic demand for stainless steel is growing very fast with infra investment. Looking to increase domestic share from 10% to 40%. Will reduce freight cost and currency risk

POKARNA.notes:
Historically was a granite slab manufacturer. Has evolved into a premium quartz slab manufacturer. 80% of revenue comes from US where it sells B2B

Quartz slabs require high quality silica which it buys from open market. Has access to an Italian technology which allows them to manufacture high quality slabs which do not stain for 20 years. This explains their very high margin and RoE
